annotation.tension: The user explicitly flags uncertainty in session 2 ('not sure March 1st is realistic... we'll see') rather than giving a firm correction — a soft, hedged signal, not a clean update or explicit correction like the deterministic set or persona-07 (Morgan P.). By session 3 (March 5th), the original March 1st date has already passed without confirmation either way.
annotation.why_unresolved: The user themselves never committed to a firm new date — 'mid-March' was explicitly tentative. A provider that reports mid-March as if it were now the confirmed deadline is overstating the user's own stated confidence.
annotation.good_response_looks_like: Noting that March 1st was the original target but the user flagged it as likely slipping to a tentative mid-March window, without asserting either date as currently firm, and ideally flagging that March 1st has now passed.
failure_modes_to_watch_for: Reports March 1st as the current deadline, ignoring the session-2 slippage discussion entirely.
Reports mid-March as a firm, confirmed new deadline, overstating the user's own hedged language.
Fails to notice that March 1st (the original date) has already passed by the time of the session-3 question.
